scenarios.title: Let the right workstation reach the vault
scenarios.summary: Use a source-only filter without blocking independent traffic in the opposite direction.
scenarios.objective: Allow Admin to reach Vault on the listed TCP 443 and ICMP checks. Block Guest on both checks as packets leave Gateway through service. Keep the independent Vault-to-Guest TCP 443 check allowed. Build Gateway's policy and verify all five outcomes; routes and addresses are supplied.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Start with the first failed traffic check. Compare its direction, first matching rule and protocol/ports, then retry. Required allowed traffic must still pass.
scenarios.explanation: A standard source permit for Admin, attached on Gateway/service out, allows both required protocols. Guest matches no permit and is denied. An explicit Guest deny followed by a permit also meets the stated flows. The independent Vault-to-Guest packet enters service, so this outbound filter does not inspect it.
hints: A standard list can decide both TCP and ICMP cases from their source address alone.
The required boundary is Gateway/service out. A denial at another boundary does not satisfy this ticket.
Permit the approved source and leave unmatched traffic to implicit deny, or explicitly deny Guest and permit the required remaining traffic.

Guest to Vault ICMP blocked at service out
Vault to Guest TCP 443 allowed independently

acl_teaching.prerequisite_note: Know an IPv4 address and how a router joins two networks. No prior ACL experience is needed; all addresses and routes are supplied.

concepts.title: Allow or block a packet
concepts.text: An access control list (ACL) is an ordered set of permit/deny rules. A standard list checks the sender's IP address only; it does not distinguish a website from other protocols. ICMP is a separate IP protocol, not a TCP/UDP port.

concepts.title: Read one small source rule
concepts.text: In the example below, permit host 10.1.4.11 permits Ada. host means one exact address; any means every address. After the last rule of a list containing rules, an unmatched packet is denied. With no list attached, these links do not filter.

concepts.title: Attach it in the correct direction
concepts.text: ip access-list standard NAME starts a named rule list; exit closes a section. interface service selects the supplied port, and ip access-group NAME out attaches that list to packets leaving toward SampleStore. Packets entering service are separate. Checking replaces the complete document; omitted sections are removed.

acl_teaching.example_description: Ada may reach SampleStore on TCP 8080 and ICMP; Bo may not. SampleStore may still send the listed TCP 8080 packet to Bo. Fill worked example, then Check example; filling alone does not run it.

cases.label: SampleStore to Bo TCP 8080 stays allowed

routers.SampleGate:
ip access-list standard sample-source
 permit host 10.1.4.11
exit
interface service
 ip access-group sample-source out
exit

try_change.description: After it passes, clear the SampleGate document and Check example. Both Bo packets become allowed because no filter is attached; Ada and the reverse packet still pass. Refill and check to repair.

scenarios.title: Repair a service exception hidden by a broad permit
scenarios.summary: Reorder an extended list while preserving protocol, source-port and return-direction guards.
scenarios.objective: Block Designer and Support TCP destination port 22 to Portal at Edge/clients in. Preserve the listed TCP 443, TCP 8443, UDP 22 and UDP 53 traffic, plus Portal's independent reverse packet. The starting broad permit hides the deny. Repair the document and verify all seven checks.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Start with the first failed traffic check. Compare its direction, first matching rule and protocol/ports, then retry. Required allowed traffic must still pass.
scenarios.explanation: The repaired sequence-10 TCP destination-22 deny runs before the broad sequence-20 IP permit. UDP 22 does not match TCP, and source port 22 is not destination port 22. The reverse packet traverses the interface in the other direction. Equivalent permits-only solutions also pass this finite task; unlisted ports are not certified by these checks.
hints: Locate the first matching row for TCP 22; a later deny cannot undo an earlier permit.
Compare the UDP 22 check and the TCP 8443 check whose source port is 22. Protocol and source/destination position matter.
Move a precise TCP destination-22 deny before the broad permit, or use equivalent supported rules that pass every listed check.

cases.label: Designer to Portal TCP 22 blocked at clients in
Support to Portal TCP 22 blocked at clients in
Portal TCP 22 source to Designer 50000 allowed

solution:
acl-author {"kind":"ApplyDocuments","documents":{"schema_version":1,"routers":{"Edge":"ip access-list extended office-services
 20 permit ip any any
 10 deny tcp any host 10.20.9.30 eq 22
exit
interface clients

acl_teaching.prerequisite_note: Use the preceding source-policy activity first, or review its introduction. Know that a port number identifies the intended service within TCP or UDP.

concepts.title: Match the service as well as the sender
concepts.text: Extended rules can check both addresses and the protocol. In deny tcp any host 172.20.8.40 eq 8080, eq 8080 follows the destination, so it tests the destination TCP port. UDP port 8080 is a different match and remains allowed here.

concepts.title: The first matching rule decides
concepts.text: A broad permit before a specific deny lets the packet through immediately; later rules are never consulted. When every row has a sequence number, smaller numbers run first, even if their text appears lower in the document.

concepts.title: Keep the required permitted traffic
concepts.text: Fixing a denied service is not enough if you also break the allowed checks. You may use explicit denies and a broader permit, or a permits-only list with implicit deny, when all stated outcomes still match.

acl_teaching.example_description: Block Maker and Helper TCP 8080 to SampleSite; keep Maker TCP 8443 and Helper UDP 8080 working. The starting broad permit shadows the deny. Fill the repaired example, then Check example.

routers.SampleEdge:
ip access-list extended sample-services
 5 deny tcp any host 172.20.8.40 eq 8080
 10 permit ip any any
exit
interface clients
 ip access-group sample-services in
exit

try_change.description: After it passes, change the deny sequence from 5 to 20 and Check example. Both TCP 8080 packets become allowed because permit sequence 10 runs first; the required permitted packets still work. Refill/check to repair.

routers.SampleEdge:
ip access-list extended sample-services
 10 permit ip any any
 20 deny tcp any host 172.20.8.40 eq 8080
exit
interface clients
 ip access-group sample-services in
exit

scenarios.title: Find the filter facing the wrong way
scenarios.summary: Investigate a two-router path and repair a binding without blocking reverse traffic.
scenarios.objective: Block Client's TCP 23 and UDP 69 packets as they enter Branch through clients. Keep Client's TCP 22/UDP 53 and Server's independent TCP 23/UDP 69 packets to Client allowed. The list exists but faces the wrong way. Diagnose and repair Branch's document; keep Campus's supplied routing and interfaces unchanged.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Start with the first failed traffic check. Compare its direction, first matching rule and protocol/ports, then retry. Required allowed traffic must still pass.
scenarios.explanation: Client traffic enters Branch/clients before routing to Campus. Binding the list in blocks the two unwanted client-originated packets there, while the allowed client protocols pass the final permit. Server's independent checks leave Branch/clients and remain unfiltered. Keeping both in and out would wrongly block those reverse cases.
hints: For a Client-to-Server packet, mark the first interface it enters on Branch. Compare the required denial location with the observed path.
The reverse checks deliberately use the same destination ports. Applying the same filter in both directions breaks them.
On Branch's clients section, replace the out attachment with in. Campus needs no new policy; equivalent rules must still enforce the stated boundary.

acl_teaching.prerequisite_note: Review source policies and extended rule order. The supplied routes already work without filtering; this task is about where and in which direction a packet is inspected.

concepts.title: Read direction from the router's viewpoint
concepts.text: clients in means a packet arriving at this router from the client link. clients out means one leaving toward the client. The same cable carries these separate directions; do not decide direction from the remote server's viewpoint.

concepts.title: Follow each one-way check
concepts.text: PracticeClient's request enters clients; PracticeService's independently tested packet leaves clients. A correct deny list attached out can miss the request while blocking the reverse check. This simulator does not infer reply/session state.

concepts.title: Move rather than duplicate the binding
concepts.text: In this complete-document editor, replace the out binding with in. Adding a second in line while retaining out leaves both filters active. Keep the list content unless a rule change is needed; Campus-style intermediate links are ordinary separate boundaries.

acl_teaching.example_description: PracticeClient TCP 2323/UDP 6969 must stop at PracticeGate/clients in. The reverse destination-2323/6969 packets and forward TCP 8443 must pass. Fill the corrected binding and Check example.

routers.PracticeGate:
ip access-list extended sample-direction
 deny tcp any any eq 2323
 deny udp any any eq 6969
 permit ip any any
exit
interface clients
 ip access-group sample-direction in
exit

try_change.description: After it passes, replace in with out on the clients binding and Check example. Both forward blocked-service checks become allowed, and both reverse checks are denied. Refill/check to restore the required direction.

routers.PracticeGate:
ip access-list extended sample-direction
 deny tcp any any eq 2323
 deny udp any any eq 6969
 permit ip any any
exit
interface clients
 ip access-group sample-direction out
exit

scenarios.title: Handover the archive and portal policies
scenarios.summary: Repair source restrictions and ordered service rules across two routers without collateral blocking.
scenarios.objective: Complete the supplied traffic table: Staff may use Archive on TCP 443, UDP 53 and TCP 22; Visitor's TCP 443/UDP 53 to Archive must stop at Core/archive out. Preserve the allowed Portal rows, but TCP 22 from either client to Portal must stop at Edge/clients in. Keep the two independent reverse checks allowed. Repair both documents and verify all 13 outcomes; routing and addresses stay fixed.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Start with the first failed traffic check. Compare its direction, first matching rule and protocol/ports, then retry. Required allowed traffic must still pass.
scenarios.explanation: Edge's corrected inbound extended list denies only TCP destination22 to Portal before its broad permit. Core's outbound Archive source list permits Staff and denies Visitor on the two required Archive checks. Portal UDP22 and Staff's Archive TCP22 distinguish the protocol/destination scopes. Independent reverse packets cross neither protected outbound/inbound direction, so they stay allowed. All current checks must pass together; fixing one router alone is partial work.
hints: Group failed checks by their required boundary. Archive source access and Portal service access are separate policy jobs.
A source list on Core/transit in also inspects Portal-bound traffic. Compare that placement with the required archive out boundary, and inspect which client's address is permitted.
On Edge, the precise Portal TCP22 rule must precede the broad permit and attach clients in. On Core, permit Staff at archive out; explicit or implicit denials are valid if every stated flow passes.

acl_teaching.prerequisite_note: Combine the preceding source, service-order and direction activities. Network routes are already correct and fixed; work on policy documents, not routing workarounds.

concepts.title: Two independent boundaries
concepts.text: A source-only list on SampleCore/archive out protects the store. An extended list on SampleEdge/clients in rejects only the listed TCP service toward the site. A source filter on the shared transit link would also affect the site, so placement matters.

concepts.title: Preserve the other service and direction
concepts.text: A TCP service deny must not accidentally block the same-numbered UDP check, the permitted destination, or independent reverse packets. No session is inferred: each displayed row is one explicit direction and protocol/port tuple.

concepts.title: Check the complete handover
concepts.text: Edit both router documents before Check configuration. All drafts apply together or none does. A blank document clears that router's modeled policy, not the other router. Every required allowed and denied row must pass from the same current network.

acl_teaching.example_description: SampleGuest must not reach SampleStore on TCP 8080/UDP 5353, while SampleStaff TCP 8080 works. Block both clients' TCP 2323 to SampleSite, keep its TCP 8443/UDP 2323 and the listed reverse packet working. Fill both documents, then Check example.

routers.SampleEdge:
ip access-list extended sample-site
 deny tcp any host 10.190.2.20 eq 2323
 permit ip any any
exit
interface clients
 ip access-group sample-site in
exit
routers.SampleCore:
ip access-list standard sample-store
 permit host 10.180.1.10
exit
interface archive
 ip access-group sample-store out
exit

try_change.description: After all checks pass, clear only SampleCore's document and Check example. The two store denials stop passing because SampleGuest now reaches it; the site service policy and all allowed checks remain correct. Refill/check both documents to repair.
